Warning: this may be long. The end happened a month ago, but the destruction of a 5 year friendship isn't something you "just get over".

Anyway. So "S" and I met at the beginning of 8th grade. She immediately liked me. A special greeting like that was very refreshing to me after the bullies I had encountered in 7th grade from my previous school. My name is the same as hers, and S has a twin, so S and I referred to each other as "name sister".

The school I started in 8th grade was small, so I spent most of my school days with her, and her twin, but I wasn't close to S's twin much. We had a ton of inside jokes. We also went special places together (my mom, her mom, her twin, and of course her and me) over the years such as theme parks, aquariums, museums, festivals, etc. We were extremely close to each other. We trusted each other completely and we told each other our secrets. I was aware that S had a friend, "V", who she had known for over ten years. But V moved away, so I didn't know her. I never felt threatened by V. Friends have other best friends.

In my junior year of high school, V moved back to our city. She went to our high school. But I still didn't know her because I did the online schooling. Gradual changes were apparent in S. She stopped wanting to hang out with me. She avoided me. We got into fights, and all of this is very out of character for S. She was a great and understanding friend. But all this was gradual, so I thought it would be possible to fix. All of a sudden, S claimed that I was "too sad and annoying". And that our texts "we're on repeat". I have depression and anxiety, so I accept that I might have been "too sad". But I fixed it. I also fixed the "repeat texts". But she still repeated texts, and killed our conversations.

She stopped putting in effort. She blamed it all on me. She complained about V kicking her dogs, about her twin, about her parents, and other stuff. I mentioned that she complained too much. She made no effort to fix it.

The last straw was near graduation. At practice, I whispered in her ear, "we need to fix this". She proceeds to yell at me and make a show in front of V. Fast forward to Grad Nite. For this, we went to a theme park the night before graduation and stayed in the park all night. She made childish comments all night such as, "V, you're my FAVE. Only you can have hair ties from me." Ok then. I got sick before we went on our first ride, and she just leaves me alone and didn't even follow me to the bathroom. Then she calls my mom and tries to defend herself by saying "Well I didn't just leave her there!"

I got better and still had a fun time with other people. At the end of the night, we started heading towards the busses. The whole group leaves me alone and I get lost, not knowing which bus I was supposed to be on. I call S and she doesn't answer. I only had her number. Finally she does and says "we are in the store". What fucking store? There's a million of them. Finally I find them, almost in tears, and start yelling at S and V for leaving me. They ignore me and walk away.

So that was it. No more of those bitches S and V. I sat through graduation and now I have no contact with S.

S's twin felt bad for me but there wasn't much she could do. Also, V is overweight, I'm thin, and she shamed me because I'm skinny. I'm not "too skinny". From what I heard, V is apparently jealous of me because I'm pretty and thin, and because S liked me so much. V is also abusing S. She's isolating her to only have her as a friend, while V has three other best friends.

TL;DR: Best friend of five years turns on me because she was manipulated by her other best friend because that girl is jealous of me. Also, she is isolating S from other friends.

Do you think that the Beatles are overrated?
True of False: The Beatles are overrated.

I think any influential band will seem overrated in retrospect if you don't understand the context their music was created in. If you heard a song from Oasis before you heard a song from The Beatles, you might assume that The Beatles were just a more pop version of Oasis, without context.
I don't think this detracts from The Beatles at all. They were a landmark band that launched so many similar styles after them.

I agree, but if you heard all of the music they influenced before you heard any of their music you might wonder what all of the fuss is about.

If you take the view somewhere in the middle of how highly people rate them, I think it falls somewhere in the middle. If there is anyone who says they weren't influential at all, they are obviously crazy or trolling. At the other end of the spectrum there are people who are biased by their subjective love of The Beatles' music.

I'm not denying that they had an influence, but I do think their influence is a little overstated when people say they "invented" rock music. That's just not true, the go-to inventor of rock music is Chuck Berry and without him, there would be no Beatles.
And they admitted to being heavily influenced by Elvis. This is going to devolve into a treatise on the evils of copyrights and patents, isn't it? ;)

Well of course it would be. but the same would be true if you heard Mozart play today. You would think he was just a conductor trying to bring back a style from 2 centuries ago. People are obviously biased by their "subjective love" but this agains fails to detract from how good they are.

I personally think they were the best band ever. They could play just about any genre and make it a hit. Paul McCartney and John Lennon were brilliant songwriters and musicians.

It's mind boggling how much of an impact they made to music in just 10 years.

compared to other icons of that era Elvis and Marilyn Monroe I don't think The Beatles are overrated. There are few people that dont like at least a few Beatles songs.

Something closer to our time for comparison it took Madonna nearly 30 years to have as many top 10 hits as the Beatles had.
You should consider the Beatles in terms of periods/albums and not as a whole.

Something most people don't realize is that they were really only an active band for 8 years. EIGHT YEARS. Their first hit, Love Me Do, came out in 62. Their last album, Let It Be, came out in 1970. They created some of the most influential, inspiring, timeless, and innovative music...in only eight years. Madonna, the Beach Boys, the Rolling Stones, etc have spent decades evolving, and developing their sound and their name.

I can't think of a single band as internationally known, accepted, and appreciated that started eight years ago, 2007.

Granted the Beatles didn't have the competition that bands nowadays do. But they also didn't have the advantage of the Internet.

There are a lot of reasons why the Beatles are what they are, and it's not by chance.

The Beatles were great at assimilating different styles of music that were being created around them, and they certainly never sold out or followed mainstream trends, but I don't think they were ever really innovators the way, say, The Kinks or The Who were.

False. They were geniuses, everything they wrote was a hit, not because they wrote it, but because it was good. No one else could keep up with them, they weren't active very long, so the sheer talent is jaw dropping how much they wrote. Yes, I love me some Beatles.

True and false. They wrote some of the best pop music ever. They managed to be rhythmically complex, artistically sound, and catchy enough to capture the limelight. That is an extraordinary feat. But, fans have a way of blowing their ingenuity out of proportion. They rarely invented anything new, but they had a knack for perfecting and commercializing what they gleaned off of records released by more underground bands of the time.
